steps.html:
Why do you go geocaching? — To keep fit.

I go to Bob's house every weekend to look after his dog.

She's going to move to Greece to teach English.

We're going to buy eggs and sugar to make a cake.

steps.title: Saying why: to + verb
steps.html:
QuestionAnswerFull sentence
Why do you go?To keep fit.I go geocaching to keep fit.
Why did he get up early?To paint.He got up early to paint the living room.
Why are you calling them?To organize a party.I'm going to call them to organize a party.

After to the verb is the base form: to keep, to make, to visit.

This works with any tense — past, present or a plan with going to.

Learners often say for keep fit or for to keep fit. It is simply to keep fit.

steps.title: Offering to help
steps.html:
FormExampleHow strong
I'll + verbI'll take notes.you have decided
Shall I + verb?Shall I write that down?you are asking
Would you like me to + verb?Would you like me to ask them?most polite
Let me + verbLet me help you with that.friendly
Why don't I + verb?Why don't I give him the list?suggesting

I'll is the short form of I will. It is what people say when they decide at that moment.

None of these takes to after the first part, except Would you like me to…
